about: G7 short answers, in SUNLINE's own words: one or two sentences per trophy, each ending with the cite numbers of the trophy's own steps or missable call it summarises. No new facts; the numbers are the same [n] the trophy's guide pane uses after the G5 merge.

answers.1: Earn the other 54 trophies in one single-player run of near 200 hours [1][3]. Cheats switch off trophies; the only flagged risk is the Chapter 1 meditation spot [1].
answers.2: Start a new game and finish the opening Chapter 1 mission; it unlocks by itself and cannot be missed [1].
answers.3: Finish the Chapter 1 story; the trophy usually pops as Chapter 2 starts [1][2]. Before leaving Chapter 1, meditate at Jason's house, a spot that exists only then [1][2].
answers.4: Play through Chapter 2; the trophy pops as Chapter 3 begins with Welcome to Vice City [1][2]. Keep a manual save from late Chapter 2, since missions cannot be replayed [2].
answers.5: Finish Chapter 3; it pops after Ocean Beach and Another Life in Chapter 4 [1]. Before Chapter 3 ends, play Race Against Yago, which is time-sensitive [2].
answers.6: Complete the Chapter 4 story; the trophy can wait until the next chapter starts [1][2]. Take the optional bank mission in Chapter 4, since the vault and armored-truck trophies hang off it [1].
answers.7: Make a manual save just before the final mission, then play it to the end [1][2]. It cannot be missed, and free roam stays open after the credits [1][2].
answers.8: Follow the story into Chapter 2 and finish Breakfast Run; it cannot be missed [1]. Keep a save from before it if you want to see it again, as missions cannot be replayed [1][2].
answers.9: Advance Chapter 3 and finish The Cartel Heist; it cannot be missed [1]. While Chapter 3 lasts, also play the time-sensitive Race Against Yago [2].
answers.10: Play Chapter 4 until Child's Play and finish it [1]. Also take the optional That's Where The Money Is..., which opens the vault trophies [1][2].
answers.11: Continue Chapter 4 until Headliners and finish it [1]. Save by hand between story missions, since none can be replayed [2].
answers.12: Finish VCIA Takedown when Chapter 4 offers it [1]. Stealing a jet at the airport is a separate trophy, Catch Me If You Can [1][2].
answers.13: Push into Chapter 5 and finish Operation Savage Glory [1]. Save by hand afterwards, before the final mission, which cannot be replayed [2].
answers.14: After the credits, work the checklist under Progress > Stats: 300 stunts, 70 of 80 challenges, 8 vaults, 39 operations and more [1][2]. Budget about 100 hours; nothing on it can be missed [1].
answers.15: Any stunt type counts; flying under bridges, 202 of them, is the quickest to farm [1][2]. Track the total under Progress and on the map's Stunt Spots layer [1][2].
answers.16: Try each of the nine activity types once: fishing, hunting, golf, shooting range, pool, hoops, an arcade game, a race and a stunt [1]. All of them stay open in free roam [1].
answers.17: Win gold on all 42 Shooting Range challenges across the 12 ranges [1][2]. Neither guide flags them, and ranges also raise Focus for Gunslinger [1][3].
answers.18: Win one drone race at each of the 14 Top Fun locations; you do not need all 42 races [1][2]. Neither guide flags it as missable [1].
answers.19: Win 20 of the 40 races PowerPyx counts; car races, race challenges and drone races all count [1]. Free roam stays open after the credits, so there is no rush [2].
answers.20: Finish the Chapter 1 mission Feng Shui, then follow Cal's purple fishing marker and his missions until you win [1]. OutputLag places it in Chapter 1; neither guide flags it [2].
answers.21: Play one arcade game to its end, on the TV at home or on a Bang For Your Buck cabinet [1]. OutputLag lists it in Chapter 1 [2].
answers.22: As Lucia, take Andy's missions from Chapter 3, starting with his text about a Belville address, and play them to the finale [1][3]. Andy does not count for Strangers & Freaks [1][2].
answers.23: After Island Dreams, find Kenton on Key Lento and search the 7 shipwrecks with the metal detector [1]. He is away after Chapter 1, but his finale stays open after the credits [1][2].
answers.24: After Chapter 2's Coffee Break, meet Billy at the Thrillbilly Mudclub and ride his strand through to Hometown Heroes [1]. Side finales stay open after the credits [2].
answers.25: Finish eight stranger strands: Kirk, Kyle, Yago and Pilot Pete count; Moses, Tyrone, Yasmani, Andy, Billy and Eddie do not [1][2]. Play Race Against Yago in Chapter 3: it may be time-sensitive [2].
answers.26: Get the Key Cloner in Chapter 3, then scan Randy's 16 cars with WAiNK and deliver each to his garage [1]. Hotel driveways in Vice Beach and Ocean Beach turn them up most [1][3].
answers.27: As Jason, finish Here, Kitty Kitty in Chapter 3 to unlock Tyrone, then clear his quests through Spin On This [1][2]. The finale stays open after the credits [2].
answers.28: Meditate at all 18 spots: 2-9 as each lead, plus balcony and Kalaga summit [1][4]. Do Jason's house in Chapter 1 and keep a save; it may go later [1][2].
answers.29: As Jason, start Bret's hunting quests after Chapter 2's Coffee Break and follow them with his SM-69 rifle [1][2]. Collect the 15 Target Decks on the way for 100% [1].
answers.30: Complete any 3 of the 18 card sets; the smallest are Backyard Wrestling (12) and Delights Dancers (18) [3]. If you pick Delights Dancers, take Vicki's card before Chapter 3 [4].
answers.31: Scan any 100 WAiNK spots (landmarks, curiosities, sculptures, tags) with D-pad Up, then R1 [1][2]. Scanning vehicles as well helps Whip It Good [1].
answers.32: Finish 50 of the 80 challenges under Progress > Challenges [1][2]. Go on to 70 if you want 100%; the list stays open after the story [1][2].
answers.33: After Coffee Break, call your partner, raise a wanted level and lose it together, for example in the train tunnel north of Ambrosia [1]. It pops once you leave the red heat zone [1][2].
answers.34: With your partner, rob three shops in a row, like the north Vice City jewelry stores, keeping the wanted state flashing [1][2]. The pop can lag 30 seconds; if not, rob a fourth [1][3][4].
answers.35: Scan 100 different vehicles with WAiNK; a scan counts without driving them [1][3]. Ordinary traffic is enough, with 557 vehicles in the game at launch [1].
answers.36: Turn on Combat Focus with L3 and R3 while aiming and drop gang guards at an illegal operation [1][2]. Police, soldiers and civilians do not count [1].
answers.37: Board a jet at a boarding bridge at VCIA gates E3 or E4, take off and fly about a kilometre away [1][2][3]. A jet parked on the airfield does not count [3].
answers.38: Take the tank from the south of Mile Zero Air Station in Mariana County [1][2]. Drive it and keep firing until the trophy appears [1][2].
answers.39: Get the Snap Gun from Yasmani's Chapter 3 Jewelry Jobs, open a store's back door with it and use the back-room safe code [1][2]. Kicking the door in sets off the alarm [1].
answers.40: Do the optional Chapter 4 mission That's Where The Money Is..., then tail security vans and rob bank vaults [1][2]. Expect four stars after each; there are 8 banks for the 5 needed [1][2].
answers.41: After the optional Chapter 4 bank mission, rob an armored truck or a bank vault, then escape [1][2]. Leaving the red heat zone or reaching a Pay 'n' Spray counts as getting away [1][3].
answers.42: Fly a fast plane over every patch of black fog until none is left [1]. Do it after the credits, when the whole map is open (our timing) [1].
answers.43: Raid one illegal operation of each of the 9 gangs, tracked under Progress > Gangs and shown as yellow icons [1][2][3]. All 39 count for 100%, and none closes after the story [1][2].
answers.44: Our reading: order a drink facing the sea at an Ocean Beach spot, trying another if one fails [1]. The trigger is unconfirmed, so a time window cannot be ruled out [2][3].
answers.45: Our reading: drive a display car out through a dealership showroom's window, or watch for it in a mission [1]. The trigger is not confirmed and may belong to a mission [2][3].
answers.46: At the bowling alley, take the watch and the Gutterball shotgun, blow the safe with sticky bombs, then lose the police [1]. It opens in Chapter 2, and the valuables respawn [1][2].
answers.47: After Coffee Break, train Jason and Lucia at the gym together, topping up with home workouts later [1]. OutputLag hedges the trigger, so treat it as likely [2].
answers.48: Turn on Criminal Profile notifications and let the count climb toward 500 in normal play [1][2]. Avoid the Irredeemable profile, which GTABase says is permanent [3].
answers.49: Our reading: fail something such as a robbery, then succeed on the second try [1]. PowerPyx guesses a second visit to the prologue's Payday Loans store, which could make it time-bound [2].
answers.50: Follow up odd events in the wilds and any UFO questline, which PowerPyx suspects is behind it [1][2]. The trigger is unknown, so a window cannot be ruled out [2].
answers.51: Ride a motorcycle and kick people as you pass, as PowerPyx suggests, ideally several in one pass [1][2]. The trigger is unconfirmed but sounds repeatable [2].
answers.52: Finish Credit Check in Chapter 3 for the Dye Pack Jammer, then sell marked bills from robberies, best to Yasmani [1][2]. The total is cumulative, so nothing is lost [1][2].
answers.53: Buy guns, car mods and tattoos, the priciest items, across Ammu-Nation, mod shops and Pay 'n' Spray [1]. Most shopping can wait until after the credits; spending adds up over time [1][2].
answers.54: Finish Daily Driver in Chapter 2, then buy all 8 garages on the Vice City Real Estate app, about $160,000 [1][2]. The 4 story garages do not count [1][2].
answers.55: Finish the Chapter 2 mission Moses, then respray and register cars at his Port Gellhorn garage [1][2]. Keep slots free; cheap cars and bikes keep the cost down [1][3].
